# Skills

My personal collection of agent skills: reusable instructions that coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others) load automatically when a task matches.

Each skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` file: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) followed by the instructions the agent follows.

## Install

Skills install straight from this repo with the [`skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) CLI. No npm package is needed.

```bash
# See what's available
npx skills@latest add <owner>/<repo> --list

# Install one skill into the current project
npx skills@latest add <owner>/<repo> --skill rust-egui-guidelines -a claude-code

# Install for your user, across all projects
npx skills@latest add <owner>/<repo> --skill rust-egui-guidelines -a claude-code -g
```

- Leave out `-a` to choose agents interactively (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, …).
- Add `--yes` to skip prompts in setup scripts.

**Project vs. global:** for codebase-specific rules like `rust-egui-guidelines`, install at project level and commit the installed folder (for Claude Code, `.claude/skills/`) so everyone working in that repo, and every agent, picks it up.

### Manage installed skills

```bash
npx skills list      # what's installed
npx skills update    # pull the latest versions from this repo
npx skills remove    # uninstall
```

### Manual install

Copy the skill folder into your agent's skills directory, e.g. for Claude Code:

```bash
# Project
cp -r skills/rust-egui-guidelines .claude/skills/

# Global
cp -r skills/rust-egui-guidelines ~/.claude/skills/
```

## Repository layout

```
skills/
  <skill-name>/
    SKILL.md        # required: frontmatter + instructions
    ...             # optional: reference files, scripts, templates
```

## Adding a skill

1. Create `skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`. Use kebab-case for the folder, matching the `name` field.
2. Start the file with frontmatter:

   ```markdown
   ---
   name: my-skill
   description: One sentence saying when an agent should use this skill.
   ---
   ```

   The `description` decides when the skill triggers, so make it say *when* to use it, not just what it is.
3. Write the instructions below the frontmatter. Keep them direct and checkable.
4. Commit and push. The skills table above is regenerated automatically from the frontmatter (or run `python3 scripts/update_readme.py` locally).
